title: An Executive Proposal that fails to move the hat is not rejected — it can still pass any time before expiry
content:
A.1.10.2.4.13.1 describes what happens when an Executive Proposal falls short: "If the executive does not accumulate sufficient SKY to 'move the hat'... it does not proceed to execution immediately; **however, it can still gain support and be executed later within the expiration window**. For official Spells, there is a 30-day expiration period after deployment. Once this period lapses, the Spell process ends."

There is therefore no moment of rejection. A proposal is either the hat, or a live challenger, or expired. Nothing in the mechanism produces a definitive "no" — only a clock running out.

The upside is resilience against transient conditions. A proposal that misses because delegates were unavailable, weight was in transit, or attention was elsewhere is not killed by that accident; it simply waits, and can pass the moment the coalition assembles.

The cost is that opposition is expensive and impermanent. Defeating a proposal means keeping enough weight on the hat for the full window, every day, while the proposer needs only one favourable moment. Vigilance must be continuous while the attempt only needs to succeed once — an asymmetry the Atlas mitigates by capping the window at 30 days (A.1.10.2.4.8.2.4 permits up to 90) rather than by adding a rejection mechanism.

It also means "the community rejected this" is never a fact the system records. Only expiry is recorded, and it is indistinguishable from abandonment, disagreement, or a proposal nobody noticed.
description: A.1.10.2.4.13.1 leaves a proposal live and accumulating support for its 30-day window, so Sky governance has no defeat state, only lapse.
